about.title: Compton Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Getting hurt on the job in Compton can leave you juggling medical appointments, missed paychecks, and a workers' compensation system that feels built for someone else. Here is the part many people never hear: workers' comp is generally your only claim against your employer, no matter who was at fault. But if a separate party contributed to your injury — a subcontractor on a shared site, the owner of the property where you were working, the maker of a defective tool, or another driver who hit you while you were making deliveries along Rosecrans Avenue or Alondra Boulevard — California allows a separate injury claim against that third party. That second claim can matter, because it may cover losses workers' comp does not. In 2025, Los Angeles County records logged 333 injury collisions inside Compton, with 484 people hurt, and some of those involved people who were simply doing their jobs. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. Tell us what happened, and we connect you with an independent attorney who reviews your situation on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Compton Workers Start With LawProactive

items.title: We look past the employer
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or driver can be held separately accountable. The attorneys we connect you with know to check for that.

items.title: Deadlines are tracked from day one
items.desc: You have 30 days to report the injury to your employer, and a third-party claim in California generally carries a two-year limit. Missing either can close doors, so timing gets addressed early.

items.title: Retaliation is not something you have to absorb
items.desc: California law prohibits your employer from punishing you for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim. If that is happening, it becomes part of the conversation with your attorney.

items.question: I was hit while driving a work van on Compton Boulevard. Is that workers' comp or a car accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' comp should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. If another driver caused the crash, that driver is a third party, and California lets you pursue a separate injury claim against them. Local records show Compton crashes cluster on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., a window when many people are still on the clock.

items.question: Can my Compton employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. Report the injury to your employer within 30 days and keep a copy of anything you submit. If you notice a demotion, cut hours, or termination afterward, mention it to the attorney you are connected with.

items.question: Does it cost anything to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service and is not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle workplace injury matters on contingency, which means no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. Whether to move forward is entirely your decision after you have talked with them.
